stem: Meera's grandmother in their village in Uttarakhand tells her that the Saptarishi (Big Dipper) and the Dhruva Tara (Pole Star) can help travellers find directions at night. Which statement about using the stars to find the North direction is correct?

options.text: The Pole Star belongs to the Saptarishi (Big Dipper) and always appears to move around the sky.
The Pole Star is part of the Little Dipper and appears to stay fixed, marking the North direction.
The Big Dipper itself always points towards the South, so it cannot help in finding North.
The Pole Star is the brightest star in the sky and can be seen from everywhere in the Southern Hemisphere.

teacher.key_rationale: The Pole Star (Dhruva Tara/Polaris) is part of the Little Dipper, appears stationary, and marks North; A swaps in the Big Dipper, C contradicts the guiding role of the Big Dipper, D overclaims visibility and brightness.
